e-15606.problem: Suppose $|\,\mathbf{a}\,|=13$ and the angle between vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ is $\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}.$ Find the scalar projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}.$
e-15606.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =|\,a\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =13\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}) \\  & =13\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{13}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-15607.knowledge_point: Calculating a Scalar Projection Using Components
e-15607.problem: Let $\mathbf{a}=\langle 3,3,-1 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 2,-7,0 \rangle.$ Find the scalar projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}.$
e-15607.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 2+3\cdot (-7)+(-1)\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-7)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =-\frac{15}{\sqrt{53}}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-15608.knowledge_point: Projecting a Vector Onto a Perpendicular Vector
e-15608.problem: Let $[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ Find the scalar projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}.$
e-15608.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{c}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0\cdot 2+0\cdot (-4)+1\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Let $a=⟨3,-1,-1⟩$ and $b=⟨4,4,2⟩.$ Find the scalar projection of $a$ onto $b.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 4+(-1)\cdot 4+(-1)\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}

after.name: Question 11
after.problem: Let $p=i-3j$ and $q=xi+2j+k.$ Given that the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q$ is $0,$ find the value of $x.$
after.worked_solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =1\cdot x+(-3)\cdot 2+0\cdot 1 \\  & =x-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ x-6 & =0 \\ x & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ x \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Given that the scalar projection of $a$ onto $b$ is $0,$ find the value of $x.$
content.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =0\cdot (-2)+(-2)\cdot x+1\cdot 2 \\  & =2-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 2-2x & =0 \\ 2x & =2 \\ x & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
